_comment: Reference copy of the unit schema (NEW_ARMY_BUILD_GUIDE.md §4.1). NOT loaded — it is not listed in index.json. Copy it to <unit-id>.json, fill it in, add the id to index.json. Delete any key you don't need; every key except id/name/points is optional.
name: Unit Name
_keywords_note: The printed KEYWORDS line can be scoped. `keywords` is what ALL MODELS carry; a modelProfile may add its own `keywords` for a model-specific list. `factionKeywords` is the separate FACTION KEYWORDS line. Copy the lines exactly as printed: the datasheet's own name is a keyword as well (core rules 02.01.01), but the app adds that from `name`, so do not list it here.
_attach_note: A datasheet is a Leader (isLeader) OR a Support unit (isSupport); a Bodyguard unit can take one of each. canLead lists what it can join either way. A Support unit MUST be attached.
_composition_note: For a squad of different models: keyed by unit size, then by modelProfile name. The model mix on the card and the number of each weapon follow it as the size changes, so it replaces modelBreakdown and a profile's fixed count. Give each profile a `plural`.

costing._comment: escalationAfter = copies up to and including this index use tiers[0]; later copies use the next/last tier. List EVERY size explicitly — 10 models is often not 2x the 5-model price.

_modelProfiles_note: A profile may carry its own invulnerableSave (and an optional invulnerableNote for an asterisked footnote) when models in the unit have different ones. Use the unit-level invulnerableSave below when they all share one.

ranged.name: Weapon Name
ranged._carriedBy_note: In a unit with `composition`, use carriedBy instead of count: the model name(s) that start with this weapon, or { "Boss Nob": 2 } when a model starts with several. Leave both off a weapon that is only taken through a wargear option.

_coreAbilities_note: An id, or {id, display} when the datasheet prints a value.
_wargearOptions_note: Swaps and add-ons ('X can be replaced with Y'). One decision per option; the FIRST choice is the printed loadout. `weapons` names a weapon or a weaponGroup; a weapon named by any choice is carried only while that choice is picked. `abilities` are wargear abilities that come with a choice.

wargearOptions._note: 'Any number of Boss Nob models can each...': model = one pick for every model of that profile. When one option replaces two weapons at once, write the choices as whole loadouts.
wargearOptions.label: Boss Nob

wargearOptions._note: 'For every 10 models in this unit, 1 model can...': per = one pick per that many models (max = how many each, default 1); per: 1 is 'any number of models can each'. Two choices make it a - / + count; hint is its small print. `points` on a choice is the datasheet's 'per Special Weapon: 5', paid by every model that takes it. Options that replace the same weapon share it automatically.
wargearOptions.label: Special Weapon

wargearOptions._note: 'This model can be equipped with up to 4 Extra Gunz' / '1 Boy model can be equipped with 1 Extra Gun' (pool: 1): pool = a fixed number of picks, whatever the unit's size.
wargearOptions.label: Extra Gun

_unitWeaponAbilities_note: 'This unit's ranged attacks have [X]' — shown on this datasheet's weapon rows and on the rest of an Attached unit. whileCalled:true = only while the unit is riled up.
_whileCalled_note: What this datasheet's own abilities add while it is riled up, listed in the card note. alwaysCalled:true = the unit is riled up permanently.

whileCalled.text: Move up to 5" instead of D6"

leaderBonus.text: Plain-language summary shown on the merged card.
